newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hydro, Elf in asset deal swap.
newsitem.headline: Hydro, Elf in asset deal swap.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA and Elf Petroleum Norge said on Thursday they had agreed to swap interests in four licences on the Norwegian continental shelf.

"The agreement further develops the...agreement signed in April, with a view to establishing a cooperation to secure future use of the Heimdal installations after the depletion of the field's gas reserves," Norsk Hydro said in a statement.
Under the deal, Elf will transfer 15 percent of licence 036, corresponding to 9.57 percent of the Heimdal installation and the operatorship to Norsk Hydro.

In addition, Elf will transfer to Hydro 10 percent of licence 102, block 25/5 -- with the exception of the Froey field -- where Elf is operator, and two percent in licence 120, block 34/7 and 34/8 (Visund) where Hydro is operator.
Norsk Hydro will transfer five percent in licence 193, block 34/11 -- the Kvitebjoern prospect -- to Elf.
Hydro said it planned to take over operatorship of Heimdal from January 1, 1998 and transfer personnel from the same date.
"The two companies' owner interests in licences in the Heimdal/Oseberg area will increase the possibilities of securing future use of the Heimdal installation," the statement said.
"An interest in block 34/11 will strengthen Elf's position in the Oseberg/Gullfaks area and with an interest in block 25/5, Hydro has strengthened its participation in the Heimdal area."
